description: Expose spec persist as a deterministic CLI (cam spec --persist <id>, stdin JSON) calling specifyIssueOnMain in-process, and rewrite the /cam-spec final persist step to pipe JSON into it instead of the inline TypeScript snippet (Layer-1 CLI-exposure, CAM-197 class).

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Bun.stdin is a BunFile; reading all of stdin as a string via the BunFile .text() method is the current, non-deprecated pattern and matches the existing runSpecWriteDocs production default (Bun.stdin.text()). No breaking changes around stdin reading.

userStories.title: Add cam spec --persist <id> in-process CLI mode with CAM_SPEC_RESULT handback
userStories.description: As the orchestrator (a read-only agent with no Task/inline-TS path), I need `echo '<json>' | cam spec --persist <id>` to call specifyIssueOnMain in-process so that persisting a grill spec is a single deterministic Bash pipe instead of a throwaway bun script importing internal code.
acceptanceCriteria: `echo '<json>' | cam spec --persist <id>` reads {spec, wsjf, blockedBy?} as JSON from stdin and calls specifyIssueOnMain with a production spawnFn+clock; the persist path makes no tmux/send-keys/pane-bootstrap/liveness calls (branch-isolation test asserts the injected spawnFn is only ever called with cmd=git, never tmux, following the runSpecWriteDocs test pattern). [oracle: bun test test/commands/spec.test.ts]
On {ok:true}: prints `CAM_SPEC_RESULT=<id> sha=<sha>` to stdout plus a human hint, and exits 0. [oracle: bun test test/commands/spec.test.ts]

On every {ok:false} reason (invalid-spec, invalid-wsjf, not-found, wrong-stage, not-open, integrity-error, diverged, detached-head, missing-main): prints a human printError with the reason (including the errors array for invalid-spec/invalid-wsjf/integrity-error) plus the machine line `CAM_SPEC_RESULT=ERROR reason=<reason>`, and exits 1; one test per reason mapping. [oracle: bun test test/commands/spec.test.ts]

Malformed stdin JSON: printError plus `CAM_SPEC_RESULT=ERROR reason=invalid-json`, exits 1 (JSON.parse fails before specifyIssueOnMain runs; specifyIssueOnMain is never called). [oracle: bun test test/commands/spec.test.ts]

ParsedSpecArgs gains a `{ mode: 'persist'; id: string }` union member; `--persist` without an id is a parse error (null); dispatchSpec gains an injectable persist branch that never calls runSpecFn or writeDocsFn (routing-isolation tests); the bare `<id>` thin-proxy and --write-docs paths stay byte-behaviorally unchanged and all existing tests stay green. [oracle: bun test test/commands/spec.test.ts]
SPEC_HELP usage/options list `--persist <id>` alongside `--write-docs <id>`. [oracle: bun index.ts spec --help | grep -q -- '--persist']
No --permission-mode flag is registered anywhere in the new code. [oracle: bun test test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/spec.ts (add runSpecPersist + SpecPersistOptions next to runSpecWriteDocs, same injection shape: readStdin/spawnFn/clock/writeStdout plus a persistFn full-bypass for branch-isolation tests); index.ts (ParsedSpecArgs union ~line 847, parseSpecArgs ~line 861, SpecDispatchDeps ~line 908, dispatchSpec ~line 927, SPEC_HELP ~line 229); test/commands/spec.test.ts (mirror the existing describe blocks: parseSpecArgs --write-docs, dispatchSpec routing isolation, runSpecWriteDocs). Gotchas: (1) specifyIssueOnMain (src/commands/issue-specify.ts:313) already validates spec+wsjf+integrity and enforces all guards; --persist must NOT re-validate, only marshal stdin and map the SpecifyIssueOnMainOutcome discriminated union. (2) sha exists only on the ok:true arm; guard the union before interpolating. (3) invalid-json is a persist-specific reason token, not a specifyIssueOnMain reason. (4) blockedBy is optional: spread it into the options only when present (exactOptionalPropertyTypes-style spreads as in _buildCreateIssueOpts, index.ts:1406). (5) Print the machine line + human hint inside runSpecPersist mirroring runSpecWriteDocs (spec.ts:260-308), not in dispatchSpec; CAM-210's dispatchIssue close/abandon (index.ts:1441-1466) is the sibling precedent for the RESULT-line wording. (6) noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array/regex-group access. (7) Never register --permission-mode. (8) Production spawnFn wrapper: spawnSync(cmd, args, {...opts, stdio: 'pipe'}) as SpawnSyncReturns<string>, same as spec.ts:266-268.

userStories.title: Rewrite /cam-spec persist final step to pipe JSON into cam spec --persist (both copies)
userStories.description: As the orchestrator running /cam-spec, I need the skill's 'Final step: persist the spec' to instruct a single-quoted-heredoc pipe into `cam spec --persist <id>` so that the persist path never again requires an inline specifyIssueOnMain snippet the orchestrator cannot execute.
acceptanceCriteria: Both copies (.claude/commands/cam-spec.md and templates/commands/cam-spec.md) replace the inline specifyIssueOnMain TypeScript snippet in 'Final step: persist the spec' with a single-quoted heredoc (<<'EOF', CAM-106 safe-quoting) piping the assembled {spec, wsjf, blockedBy?} JSON into `cam spec --persist <id>`, and instruct never using an unquoted heredoc/echo (mirroring the --write-docs step's safe-quoting prose). [oracle: grep -q "cam spec --persist" .claude/commands/cam-spec.md && grep -q "cam spec --persist" templates/commands/cam-spec.md && ! grep -q "import { specifyIssueOnMain" .claude/commands/cam-spec.md && ! grep -q "import { specifyIssueOnMain" templates/commands/cam-spec.md]

The rewritten step documents the handback contract: success is `CAM_SPEC_RESULT=<id> sha=<sha>` (exit 0); any failure prints `CAM_SPEC_RESULT=ERROR reason=<reason>` (exit 1) and the orchestrator must stop and report, never retry silently; the error-handling table maps the guard reasons to the CLI's ERROR line instead of 'the guard error from specifyIssueOnMain'. [oracle: grep -q 'CAM_SPEC_RESULT' .claude/commands/cam-spec.md && grep -q 'CAM_SPEC_RESULT' templates/commands/cam-spec.md]

The separate 'Final step: persist the domain docs' (`cam spec --write-docs <id>`) stays a distinct, unchanged command/step (decision A: persist and write-docs are two pipes). [oracle: grep -q 'cam spec --write-docs' .claude/commands/cam-spec.md && grep -q 'cam spec --write-docs' templates/commands/cam-spec.md]
The two copies remain byte-identical to each other (they are today; verified via diff before this plan). [oracle: diff .claude/commands/cam-spec.md templates/commands/cam-spec.md]
Vendor drift check passes after re-embedding (bun run embed-vendor, then the check). [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: .claude/commands/cam-spec.md (persist step at lines 32-56; overview line 7 mentions 'calls the deterministic spec writer (specifyIssueOnMain)' and should reference the CLI; error-handling table line ~131), templates/commands/cam-spec.md (byte-identical twin), src/vendor/_generated.ts (regenerated, never hand-edited). Gotchas: (1) /cam-spec is per-file dual-copy; edit BOTH and keep them identical; templates/commands/cam-spec.md is embedded at build time, so run `bun run embed-vendor` to regenerate src/vendor/_generated.ts and let embed-vendor:check prove no drift. (2) Use <<'EOF' (quoted delimiter) in every example so operator answer content cannot be shell-interpolated (CAM-106). (3) Persisted .md follows the no-em-dash project rule; do not introduce em-dashes in the rewritten prose. (4) The bare `cam spec <id>` thin-proxy description (line 3) stays untouched; only the persist final-step and its cross-references change. (5) Model the handback-parsing prose on the /cam-issue Step 3 output contract (CAM_ISSUE_RESULT grep line).
